preconditions.description: n is the number of cities (4 ≤ n ≤ 1000), and k is the maximum allowed roads (n-1 ≤ k ≤ 2n-2).

preconditions.expression: len(a_b_c_d) == 4 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in a_b_c_d) and len(set(a_b_c_d)) == 4
preconditions.description: a, b, c, d are four distinct integers between 1 and n (inclusive), representing cities.
There is no direct road between a and b, and no direct road between c and d (implied by the problem statement).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (len(v_path) == n and len(u_path) == n and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in v_path) and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in u_path))
postconditions.description: If possible, output consists of two lines: the first line is a path v_1, ..., v_n where v_1 = a and v_n = b, and the second line is a path u_1, ..., u_n where u_1 = c and u_n = d. Otherwise, output is '-1'.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and all(v_path[i] != v_path[j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n)) and all(u_path[i] != u_path[j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n))
postconditions.description: Both paths contain all n cities exactly once (no duplicates).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and v_path[0] == a and v_path[-1] == b and u_path[0] == c and u_path[-1] == d
postconditions.description: The first path starts at a and ends at b, and the second path starts at c and ends at d.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and len(set((v_path[i], v_path[i + 1]) for i in range(n - 1)) | set((u_path[i], u_path[i + 1]) for i in range(n - 1))) <= k
postconditions.description: The total number of distinct roads (undirected edges) used in both paths is at most k.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and not any((v_path[i], v_path[i + 1]) == (a, b) or (v_path[i], v_path[i + 1]) == (b, a) for i in range(n - 1)) and not any((u_path[i], u_path[i + 1]) == (c, d) or (u_path[i], u_path[i + 1]) == (d, c) for i in range(n - 1))
postconditions.description: Neither path contains a direct road between a and b or between c and d (as per problem statement).
